name: Mint-Coriander Chutney
subtitle: the sharp green chutney that goes with everything fried

ingredients.note: leaves only: the stalks are bitter

prepNotes: Use mint leaves only but coriander stalks and all. Mint stalks are bitter; coriander stalks carry most of the flavour.
Blend with ice-cold water. Heat from the blade is what turns the chutney brown.

steps.text: Pick the mint leaves off the stalks. Wash both herbs and shake dry.
Put everything in the blender with 3 or 4 ice cubes and the lemon juice.
steps.tip: The ice keeps the blade cool and the colour bright green.

steps.text: Blend in short bursts, scraping down, until smooth. Add as little water as you can.
Taste for salt, sourness and heat, and adjust; it should be sharper than seems comfortable on its own.
steps.tip: It is eaten with fried food, so it needs to cut through.

steps.text: Store in a jar with a film of oil on top if keeping more than a day.

storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated in a sealed jar and freezes well in ice cube trays for 3 months. It darkens after a day but the flavour holds.
